title: Watching, private inbox and notification delivery
summary: Canonical owner of watch/unwatch. Event creation, preference and worker behavior are documented independently from external SMTP delivery. Related test files are references only; no tests were executed for this inventory.

cases.title: Preserve mail commit uncertainty
preconditions: The actor is active and approved; issue notifications refer to currently accessible project content unless a denial case states otherwise.
steps: Allow a real local SMTP sink to acknowledge the owned DATA payload, hold only that delivery’s QUIT response, and kill only the owned secondary worker with SIGKILL before Send returns or its database transaction commits.
Observe the retained pending row, then restart the captured server and let it retry the same delivery.
expected: The acknowledged external SMTP acceptance is not rolled back with the database transaction: the retained row remains pending with attempt 0 after the crash.
The retry may be acknowledged a second time with the same stable Message-ID, then persist sent with attempt 1; this demonstrates at-least-once mail and does not promise duplicate suppression.
notes: This case documents the send-before-commit boundary, not a guarantee of duplicate suppression.
Local acceptance clarifies crash-before-commit rather than claiming a PostgreSQL COMMIT error was injected. Intended-provider receipt remains a separate pending acceptance target.
A SIGKILL can prevent Go coverage counter flushing for that child; runtime case evidence and measured source coverage must be reported separately.

The real local SMTP integration now verifies accepted DATA followed by owned-worker SIGKILL, retained pending attempt 0, and a second accepted delivery with the same Message-ID before sent attempt 1. The inherent at-least-once boundary remains documented; intended-provider acceptance remains pending separately.
